english: I think I'm going to decide which animal it is after I'm done.
french: Je crois que je déciderai de quel animal il s'agit quand j'aurai terminé.
russian: Думаю, я решу, что это будет за животное, когда закончу.
bulgarian: I think I'm going to decide which animal it is after I'm done.

english: I'm working on something new, but the way it's going...

russian: Работаю над кое-чем новым, но получается что-то...
bulgarian: I'm working on something new, but the way it's going...

english: Everything I know about whittling, I learned by making myself a nuisance to Landen when I was a kid!
french: Tout ce que je sais sur le travail du bois, je l'ai appris dans ma jeunesse en passant mes journées à enquiquiner Landen !
russian: Всё, что я знаю о резьбе по дереву, я узнал, досаждая Ландену в детстве!
bulgarian: Everything I know about whittling, I learned by making myself a nuisance to Landen when I was a kid!

Привет,

соседи

соседкасоседсосед!

english: A bath was just the thing!
french: J'avais bien besoin d'un bon bain !
russian: Вот эта банька — то, что надо!
bulgarian: A bath was just the thing!

english: You know, I told Luc that bees can fly in the rain because of their yellow jackets.
french: Tu sais, j'ai raconté à Luc que les abeilles pouvaient voler sous la pluie grâce à leur ciré jaune.
russian: Я тут Люку сказал: пчёлам дождь не помеха — они одеты в жёлтые дождевички!
bulgarian: You know, I told Luc that bees can fly in the rain because of their yellow jackets.

english: You look tired, [Ari]... take a break, have a bite to eat. No one would accuse you of loafing around.
french: Tu as l'air fatigué<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they>, [Ari]... Fais une pause pour manger un morceau. Personne ne t'accusera de flemmarder.
russian: Ты выглядишь устало, [Ari]... Сделай перерыв, перекуси. Никто не подумает, что ты бездельничаешь.
bulgarian: You look tired, [Ari]... take a break, have a bite to eat. No one would accuse you of loafing around.

english: Nora was going to skip breakfast, but I talked her out of it. It's true what they say... breakfast is butter together!
french: Nora voulait se passer de petit-déjeuner, mais je le lui ai déconseillé. Finalement, elle s'est exécutée sans bruncher.
russian: Нора хотела пропустить завтрак, но я её отговорил. Я всегда говорю: позавтракал с маслом — и весь день как по маслу!
bulgarian: Nora was going to skip breakfast, but I talked her out of it. It's true what they say... breakfast is butter together!

english: Crunch crunch... oh, [Ari]! You didn't see me eating on the job, okay? I have to destroy the evidence! CRUNCH CRUNCH CRUNCH!
french: Crounch, crounch... Oh, [Ari] ! Tu ne m'as pas vu grignoter au travail, on est d'accord ? Je fais disparaître toutes les preuves... CROUNCH, CROUNCH, CROUNCH !
russian: Хрум-хрум... ой, [Ari]! Только никому не говори, что я ем на работе, ладно? Надо уничтожить улики! ХРУМ-ХРУМ-ХРУМ!
bulgarian: Crunch crunch... oh, [Ari]! You didn't see me eating on the job, okay? I have to destroy the evidence! CRUNCH CRUNCH CRUNCH!

english: I had a great weekend! Finally carved out some time to do some whittling!
french: J'ai passé un super week-end ! J'ai eu le temps de bûcher sur mes sculptures sur bois !
russian: Отличные были выходные! Наконец-то выкроил время для резьбы по дереву!
bulgarian: I had a great weekend! Finally carved out some time to do some whittling!

english: It's a quick way of Celine my fate.
french: Elle est du genre « Dell »-icate.
russian: А то ещё стану удобрением для её цветочков!
bulgarian: It's a quick way of Celine my fate.

english: I try not to make dad jokes when my eldest is around.
french: J'essaie de ne pas faire des jeux de mots pourris quand la petite est dans le coin.
russian: Стараюсь не отпускать папашкины шуточки при старшей.
bulgarian: I try not to make dad jokes when my eldest is around.

english: Hope Celine's settling into her cottage alright.
french: J'espère que Céline se sent bien dans sa petite bicoque.
russian: Надеюсь, Селин хорошо обустроилась в своём домике.
bulgarian: Hope Celine's settling into her cottage alright.

english: Pardon me, [Ari]! Just cleaning up.
french: Excuse-moi, [Ari]. Je fais juste un peu de ménage.
russian: Извини, [Ari]! Просто тут прибираюсь.
bulgarian: Pardon me, [Ari]! Just cleaning up.

english: Coffee's got it tough at our place. Imagine getting mugged every morning!
french: Le matin, je m'enfile plusieurs tasses de café pour éviter d'être moulu le reste de la journée.
russian: Кофе тяжело быть нашим соседом. Мы его каждре утро заливаем!
bulgarian: Coffee's got it tough at our place. Imagine getting mugged every morning!

english: Reminds me of Nora at her age.
french: J'ai l'impression de revoir Nora au même âge.
russian: Прям как Нора в её возрасте.
bulgarian: Reminds me of Nora at her age.

english: Dell would rather be out adventuring than making her bed.
french: Dell préfère partir à l'aventure toute la journée que faire son lit.
russian: Делл бы лучше пошла в поход, чем кровать застилала.
bulgarian: Dell would rather be out adventuring than making her bed.

english: How can Dell possibly be so muddy this early in the day? I'm honestly a little impressed.
french: Comment Dell peut-elle être si crasseuse si tôt dans la journée ? À vrai dire, je suis impressionné.
russian: Как Делл умудрилась так испачкаться с самого утра? Если честно, это даже впечатляет.
bulgarian: How can Dell possibly be so muddy this early in the day? I'm honestly a little impressed.

english: Nora likes savory, Dell likes sweet, and Celine likes her veggies... dinner is a real free-for-all at our place.
french: Nora aime le salé, Dell le sucré, et Céline est plutôt légumes... Chez nous, il y en a pour tous les goûts au dîner.
russian: Норе по вкусу солёное, Делл любит сладкое, а Селин ест овощи... Ужин у нас — буквально сборная солянка.
bulgarian: Nora likes savory, Dell likes sweet, and Celine likes her veggies... dinner is a real free-for-all at our place.

english: What a beautiful day! I wonder if anyone's down by the Beach.
french: Quelle magnifique journée ! Je me demande s'il y a du monde à la plage.
russian: Какой чудесный день! Интересно, кто-то есть на пляже?
bulgarian: What a beautiful day! I wonder if anyone's down by the Beach.

english: Finally, my favorite season has arrived! It's a Winter Pun-derland!
french: Ma saison préférée est enfin arrivée ! L'hiver est propice aux jeux de mots divers !
russian: Наконец-то моё любимое время года — зимняя спячка!
bulgarian: Finally, my favorite season has arrived! It's a Winter Pun-derland!

english: Wow, listen to Elsie go!
french: Waouh, Elsie a vraiment une jolie voix !
russian: Вот это Элси даёт!
bulgarian: Wow, listen to Elsie go!

english: You know, I'm supposed to be doing chores out here, and I am, but mostly I'm enjoying the weather. It's beauti-fall out here!
french: Tu sais, j'ai toujours du travail à faire, mais je passe pas mal de temps à admirer tout ce qui m'entoure. L'automne n'est jamais monotone !
russian: Я вроде как делами занялся на улице, но если честно — просто наслаждаюсь погодой. Ну осень крачиво!
bulgarian: You know, I'm supposed to be doing chores out here, and I am, but mostly I'm enjoying the weather. It's beauti-fall out here!

english: After spending all day on my feet, it's nice to take a load off! There's always an open seat at the Sleeping Dragon.
french: Comme c'est agréable de décompresser après avoir passé toute la journée debout ! Il y a toujours un siège où s'asseoir à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort.
russian: После целого дня на ногах приятно сесть отдохнуть! В «Спящем драконе» всегда найдётся место.
bulgarian: After spending all day on my feet, it's nice to take a load off! There's always an open seat at the Sleeping Dragon.

english: How's that fall weather treating you? Having a gourd day?
french: Alors, ça se passe bien, cet automne ? Tu te prépares à hiberner ?
russian: Как тебе осень, [Ari]? Тыковка не мёрзнет?
bulgarian: How's that fall weather treating you? Having a gourd day?

english: Nice to meet you, [Ari], I'm Holt. I'd been wondering who'd moo-ve into that old farm.
french: Content de faire ta connaissance, [Ari]. Moi c'est Holt. Je me demandais qui avait vache-ment envie de s'installer dans cette vieille ferme.
russian: Приятно познакомиться, [Ari]. Я Хольт. Всё думал, кто же посеется на той старой ферме.
bulgarian: Nice to meet you, [Ari], I'm Holt. I'd been wondering who'd moo-ve into that old farm.

english: Ahahaha...
french: Ah-ha-ha-ha...
russian: Ах-ха-ха...
bulgarian: Ahahaha...

english: I'm peas-ed to meet you too, Holt!
french: En-chantier de te rencontrer, Holt.
russian: Приятно познако-комиться, Хольт!
bulgarian: I'm peas-ed to meet you too, Holt!

english: Yes... well uh...
french: Oui... eh bien, euh...
russian: Эм... ну да...
bulgarian: Yes... well uh...

english: Haha! That's a good one!
french: Ha ha ! Elle est bien bonne !
russian: Ха-ха! Неплохо, неплохо!
bulgarian: Haha! That's a good one!

english: What's the matter? It be-hooves you to respond to a pun in kind, you know.
french: Et ben alors ? Il est d'usage de répondre à une blague de la meuh-me façon, tu sais.
russian: Что такое? У нас принято отвечать уткой на шутку. Или шуткой на утку.
bulgarian: What's the matter? It be-hooves you to respond to a pun in kind, you know.

english: Don't worry, I'll help you practice. You'll get the hang of it!
french: Ne t'inquiète pas, je t'aiderai à t'entraîner. Tu prendras le coup !
russian: Но не переживай. Я помогу тебе потренироваться. А потом само станет получаться!
bulgarian: Don't worry, I'll help you practice. You'll get the hang of it!

english: Anywho, my wife Nora and I run the $General Store$. Our girls, Celine and Dell, help out as well. Stop by if you ever need supplies!
french: Quoi qu'il en soit, je gère avec ma femme, Nora, le $magasin général$. Nos filles, Céline et Dell, nous donnent aussi un coup de main. Passe nous voir si tu as besoin de marchandises !
russian: Как бы там ни было, мы с Норой держим $универмаг$. Наши девочки, Селин и Делл, тоже в деле. Заходи, если что-то понадобится!
bulgarian: Anywho, my wife Nora and I run the $General Store$. Our girls, Celine and Dell, help out as well. Stop by if you ever need supplies!

english: Well hello there. You must be the new face in town!
french: Tiens, bonjour. C'est sans doute toi, la nouvelle tête au village !

Ну привет! Значит, ты у нас в городе

новенькие

новенькаяновенькийновенькое.

russian: Если что-то нужно — просто скажи, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Let me know if there's anything I can help you with, [Ari]!

english: Time to make like a pitchfork and hit the hay!
french: Il est l'heure de rouler la viande dans le torchon !
russian: Пора на боковую!
bulgarian: Time to make like a pitchfork and hit the hay!

english: I try to keep the house tidy, but it's hard when Hurricane Dell tears through every night. Haha!
french: J'essaie de garder la maison propre, mais ce n'est pas toujours facile quand la tempête Dell passe chaque soir. Ha ha !
russian: Стараюсь держать дом в порядке, но когда каждый вечер тут проносится ураган Делл, это не легкая задача! Ха-ха!
bulgarian: I try to keep the house tidy, but it's hard when Hurricane Dell tears through every night. Haha!

english: It just smells so good in here!
french: Ce n'est pas de ma faute, ça sent toujours si bon, ici !
russian: Тут так вкусно пахнет!
bulgarian: It just smells so good in here!

english: I always drop by to say good morning and end up staying for a bite.
french: Je passe chaque matin dire bonjour, mais je finis par rester pour manger un morceau.
russian: Часто захожу просто поздороваться, а в итоге всегда остаюсь перекусить.
bulgarian: I always drop by to say good morning and end up staying for a bite.

english: When the Inn gets real crowded, sometimes Jo and Hemlock will croon for the guests.
french: Quand il y a beaucoup de monde à l'auberge, il arrive que Jo et Hemlock poussent la chansonnette pour les invités.
russian: Когда в трактире много народу, Джо и Хемлок иногда поют для гостей.
bulgarian: When the Inn gets real crowded, sometimes Jo and Hemlock will croon for the guests.

english: Sounds like the kids had a lot of fun at the Beach today. Have you been out there, [Ari]? Summer's the season for it.
french: Apparemment, les enfants se sont bien amusés à la plage aujourd'hui. Tu y vas de temps en temps, [Ari] ? L'été est la saison idéale pour ça.

Похоже, дети хорошо провели время на пляже. А ты

были

былабылбыло там, [Ari]? Лето ведь создано для этого.

english: That project kept him busy for months.

russian: Этот проект занял у него месяцы.
bulgarian: That project kept him busy for months.

english: Fun fact: Landen built all the shelving and display cases in here!
french: C'est Landen qui a construit toutes les étagères et tous les présentoirs que tu vois ici ! Tu étais au courant ?
russian: Забавный факт: все полки и витрины здесь построил Ланден!
bulgarian: Fun fact: Landen built all the shelving and display cases in here!

english: When I do it, it doesn't make any cents!
french: Mais comme elle gère, je ne me fais pas de bilan.
russian: А когда я пытаюсь, всё время как-то не складывается!
bulgarian: When I do it, it doesn't make any cents!

english: I love my job. I tried doing what Nora does, but she's the one with the head for accounting.
french: J'adore mon boulot. J'ai bien essayé d'aider Nora pour la compta, mais elle est bien plus douée pour ça que moi.
russian: Я люблю свою работу. Пробовал заниматься тем, что делает Нора, но это у неё талант считать.
bulgarian: I love my job. I tried doing what Nora does, but she's the one with the head for accounting.

english: It's been quieter since Celine moved out, but Dell makes enough mess for both of them.
french: C'est plus calme depuis que Céline a quitté la maison, mais Dell met suffisamment de bazar pour elles deux.
russian: С тех пор, как Селин съехала, стало потише... но Делл компенсирует за двоих.
bulgarian: It's been quieter since Celine moved out, but Dell makes enough mess for both of them.

english: We got some nice stuff in this week, [Ari]! Have a look!
french: Nous avons reçu des tas de choses intéressantes, cette semaine. Jette donc un œil, [Ari] !
russian: На этой неделе у нас отличные товары, [Ari]! Загляни!
bulgarian: We got some nice stuff in this week, [Ari]! Have a look!

english: Phew... Nora's always up so early. I dawn get it.
french: Pfiou... Nora se lève toujours aux aurores. Perso, c'est l'horreur.
russian: Фух... Нора встаёт так рано. Мне такое даже не снилось.
bulgarian: Phew... Nora's always up so early. I dawn get it.

english: Turned out she secretly liked me... don't tell her, but I think it's pretty cute.
french: En réalité, elle en pinçait pour moi en secret... Ne lui répète pas, mais je trouve ça adorable.
russian: Оказалось, я ей просто нравился... Только не говори ей, но мне это до сих пор кажется милым.
bulgarian: Turned out she secretly liked me... don't tell her, but I think it's pretty cute.

english: Y'know, Nora used to pick on me when we were kids.
french: Tu sais, Nora se moquait souvent de moi quand nous étions jeunes.
russian: Знаешь, Нора в детстве меня дразнила.
bulgarian: Y'know, Nora used to pick on me when we were kids.

english: Shh, Nora's got her head in the numbers.
french: Chut, Nora est plongée dans les chiffres.
russian: Тсс, у Норы голова вся в цифрах.
bulgarian: Shh, Nora's got her head in the numbers.

english: Our fall produce is looking pretty good, [Ari]. Have yourself a look!
french: Nos produits d'automne sont alléchants. Regarde si quelque chose t'intéresse, [Ari] !
russian: Осенние овощи в этом году просто загляденье, [Ari]. Посмотри!
bulgarian: Our fall produce is looking pretty good, [Ari]. Have yourself a look!

english: Getting an early start too, [Ari]? You know what they say about early risers, right? If not, I'll wait for it to dawn on you!
french: Tu es bien matinal<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they>, [Ari] ! Tu sais ce qu'on dit des gens qui se lèvent à l'aube ? Non ? Tu l'apprendras tôt ou tard.
russian: Ты тоже с утра пораньше, [Ari]? Говорят же: кто рано встаёт... впрочем, подожду, пока само дойдёт!
bulgarian: Getting an early start too, [Ari]? You know what they say about early risers, right? If not, I'll wait for it to dawn on you!

english: Think I heard Dell conk out, we'd better keep it down out here... haha.
french: Je crois que Dell s'est enfin endormie, on ferait mieux de ne pas faire de bruit... Ha ha.
russian: Кажется, Делл уже отправилась в приключения в сонное царство, так что лучше потише... ха-ха.
bulgarian: Think I heard Dell conk out, we'd better keep it down out here... haha.

english: Never mind, it's tearable.
french: Elle risque de te faire tiquer.
russian: Обещаю, она кассная!
bulgarian: Never mind, it's tearable.

english: Do you want to hear a joke about receipts?
french: Tu connais la blague des tickets de caisse ?
russian: Хочешь шутку про чеки?
bulgarian: Do you want to hear a joke about receipts?

english: Hey [Ari]! I'm holding down the fort today. What can I get for you?
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! C'est moi qui gère, aujourd'hui. Qu'est-ce que je peux faire pour toi ?
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Сегодня я за старшего. Чем могу помочь?
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]! I'm holding down the fort today. What can I get for you?

english: We got fruits, we got vegetables, we got seeds, what else could you need?
french: Nous avons des fruits, des légumes, des semis... Il te fallait autre chose ?
russian: У нас есть фрукты, овощи, семена — а что ещё нужно-то?
bulgarian: We got fruits, we got vegetables, we got seeds, what else could you need?

english: It's [Ari], my favorite customer! Take your time, look around, let me know if you need something!
french: Mais c'est [Ari], notre <he>client préféré</he><she>cliente préférée</she><they>client·e préféré·e</they> ! Dis-moi si quelque chose attire ton attention !

Это же [Ari],

мои любимые покупатели

моя любимая покупательницамой любимый покупательмоё любимое покупатель! Осмотрись, не спеши. Если что — обращайся!
bulgarian: It's [Ari], my favorite customer! Take your time, look around, let me know if you need something!

english: Are you looking for cabbage? Turnips? Let me know if I can produce anything for you.
french: Tu veux du chou ? Ou des navets, peut-être ? Tous nos produits sont aussi cultivés que moi !
russian: Ищешь капусту? Репу? Только скажи, и я тут же вырыщу.
bulgarian: Are you looking for cabbage? Turnips? Let me know if I can produce anything for you.

english: A little grocery tip: if you're buying cabbages, two heads are better than one.
french: Laisse-moi te donner une petite astuce d'épicier : quand tu achètes des légumes, inutile de te prendre le chou.
russian: Совет по хозяйству: знаешь, почему нужно ходить в магазин за продуктами? По кочану и по капусте!
bulgarian: A little grocery tip: if you're buying cabbages, two heads are better than one.

english: Let me know if I can help you find anything, [Ari].
french: Dis-moi si je peux t'aider à quoi que ce soit, [Ari].
russian: Если что-то ищешь, [Ari], — дай знать, помогу!
bulgarian: Let me know if I can help you find anything, [Ari].

english: Don't mind me, I'm just getting the till in order. Let me know if I can help with something!
french: Ne t'occupe pas de moi. Je fais ma caisse. Si tu as besoin de quelque chose, n'hésite pas à demander !

bulgarian: Don't mind me, I'm just getting the till in order. Let me know if I can help with something!

english: The Inn is always bustling on rainy days, so Reina comes in early to stock up for the evening rush at the Inn!

bulgarian: The Inn is always bustling on rainy days, so Reina comes in early to stock up for the evening rush at the Inn!

english: Relieved of duty! Nora's got the till, if you need anything.
french: J'ai fini ma journée ! Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, c'est Nora qui tient la caisse.
russian: Свободен от дежурства! Если что нужно — Нора у кассы.
bulgarian: Relieved of duty! Nora's got the till, if you need anything.

english: Because if we didn't, we'd be ashamed of ourshelves.
french: Car ici, même nos prix sont nets !
russian: Потому что иначе нам было бы за семя!
bulgarian: Because if we didn't, we'd be ashamed of ourshelves.

english: Do you know why we keep the store so clean?
french: Sais-tu pourquoi notre magasin est toujours aussi propre ?
russian: Знаешь, почему у нас тут всегда чисто?
bulgarian: Do you know why we keep the store so clean?

english: It's a ground-breaking invention.
french: C'est l'appel de la terre, [Ari].
russian: Смеяться нужно на слове «лопата».
bulgarian: It's a ground-breaking invention.

english: Every farmer needs a shovel, eh [Ari]?
french: Tout fermier digne de ce nom se doit d'avoir une pelle.
russian: Каждому фермеру нужна лопата, да, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Every farmer needs a shovel, eh [Ari]?

english: Between you and me, it takes every bit of my willpower not to start a snowball fight.
french: Entre nous, j'ai un mal fou à ne pas démarrer une bataille de boules de neige.
russian: Между нами, я с трудом сдерживаюсь, чтобы не начать битву снежками.
bulgarian: Between you and me, it takes every bit of my willpower not to start a snowball fight.

english: The best thing about the Sleeping Dragon is that the soup's always on!
french: Ce que j'adore à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort, c'est qu'il y a toujours un bon potage chaud !
russian: Лучшее в «Спящем драконе» — суп всегда наготове!
bulgarian: The best thing about the Sleeping Dragon is that the soup's always on!

english: He'll get spoiled milk.
french: Car le jour où il arrête, elles risquent de ruminer.
russian: А то они будут давать испорченное молоко.
bulgarian: He'll get spoiled milk.

english: I keep trying to tell Hayden, he shouldn't pamper his cows too much.
french: Je dis toujours à Hayden d'essayer de ne pas trop choyer ses vaches.
russian: Пытаюсь убедить Хейдена, что не стоит чересчур баловать коров.
bulgarian: I keep trying to tell Hayden, he shouldn't pamper his cows too much.

english: I'm not much for summer, fall and winter cleaning either!
french: Ceux d'été, d'automne ou d'hiver non plus, d'ailleurs.
russian: Хотя, если честно, — ни летней, ни осенней, ни зимней тоже!
bulgarian: I'm not much for summer, fall and winter cleaning either!

english: I can't say I'm much for spring cleaning.
french: Le ménage de printemps, ça n'est pas trop mon truc.
russian: Я не любитель весенней уборки.
bulgarian: I can't say I'm much for spring cleaning.

english: Nora brought some stew back from the Inn... that family is too kind to us!
french: Nora nous a rapporté du ragoût de l'auberge... Joséphine et sa famille sont vraiment trop gentilles.
russian: Нора принесла рагу из трактира... их семья слишком добра к нам!
bulgarian: Nora brought some stew back from the Inn... that family is too kind to us!

english: Nora gave me a hard time about overstocking the shelves the other day. I told her aisle weight for an explanation.
french: Nora m'a enguirlandé pour avoir trop rempli les étagères, l'autre jour. Ce n'était pourtant que des boîtes de petits poids.
russian: На днях Нора ругалась, что я перегрузил полки. Нагрузила меня по полной!
bulgarian: Nora gave me a hard time about overstocking the shelves the other day. I told her aisle weight for an explanation.

english: Stocking up for the storm, [Ari]? I bet the Inn'll be real crowded tonight if you're looking for heaping helpings and cozy company!
french: Tu fais des provisions pour la tempête, [Ari] ? L'auberge sera sûrement pleine à craquer ce soir, si jamais tu veux te remplir la panse en bonne compagnie.
russian: Закупаешься перед бурей, [Ari]? В трактире сегодня будет не протолкнуться: и еды и уюта вдоволь!
bulgarian: Stocking up for the storm, [Ari]? I bet the Inn'll be real crowded tonight if you're looking for heaping helpings and cozy company!

english: Fall is a wonderful time of year, because I get to break out the ol' sweater vest!
french: J'adore l'automne. C'est la période où je peux ressortir ma doudoune sans manches !
russian: Осень — прекрасная пора: можно достать свой старый жилетик!
bulgarian: Fall is a wonderful time of year, because I get to break out the ol' sweater vest!

english: It's like I was maid for her!
french: Autant dire que je ne ménage pas mes efforts !
russian: Из её поля зрения!
bulgarian: It's like I was maid for her!

english: I take care of cleaning while Nora manages the General Store.
french: Je m'occupe du ménage pendant que Nora gère le magasin.
russian: Пока Нора присматривает за прилавком, я убираюсь.
bulgarian: I take care of cleaning while Nora manages the General Store.

english: Best way to wake up on thyme.
french: Cela donne bon thym !
russian: Подёргай сныть — получится у-сныть.
bulgarian: Best way to wake up on thyme.

english: I always tell Celine that if she's having trouble sleeping, she ought to take a nap in her garden.
french: Je dis toujours à Céline que si elle n'arrive pas à trouver le sommeil, rien ne vaut une petite sieste dans le jardin.
russian: Я всегда говорю Селин: не можешь спать — займись садом.
bulgarian: I always tell Celine that if she's having trouble sleeping, she ought to take a nap in her garden.

english: A tidy shop is a happy shop!
french: Un magasin bien tenu est un magasin où les gens se sentent bienvenus !
russian: Аккуратный магазин — счастливый магазин!
bulgarian: A tidy shop is a happy shop!

english: She'd fall asleep in the middle of potting her sprouts and use a sack of potting soil as a pillow. Dirt all over the carpets!
french: Il lui arrivait de s'endormir en rempotant ses plantes et d'utiliser un sac de terreau comme oreiller. Il y avait de la terre partout !
russian: Она могла уснуть прямо посреди пересадки ростков — с мешком земли под головой. Весь дом потом в грязи!
bulgarian: She'd fall asleep in the middle of potting her sprouts and use a sack of potting soil as a pillow. Dirt all over the carpets!

english: I'm tidying up while I can! Dell's the messiest now, but when Celine was little she was twice the menace Dell is.
french: Je profite que Dell n'est pas là pour range run peu. Ceci dit, quand Céline était petite, elle était encore plus compliquée que sa sœur !
russian: Пока есть время, привожу всё в порядок! Сейчас Делл — главный источник хаоса, но Селин в детстве была вдвое хуже.
bulgarian: I'm tidying up while I can! Dell's the messiest now, but when Celine was little she was twice the menace Dell is.

english: A good day of cleaning always makes me feel wiped out.
french: Après une journée entière à faire le ménage, je suis lessivé.
russian: После хорошей уборки чувствуешь себя... протёртым и выжатым.
bulgarian: A good day of cleaning always makes me feel wiped out.

english: Wonder if Landen's around... I want to up my carving technique, and he's the expert.
french: Je me demande si Landen est dans les parages... J'aimerais améliorer ma technique de sculpture sur bois, mais c'est lui l'expert.
russian: Интересно, Ланден дома? Хочу подтянуть навык резьбы: он в этом мастер.
bulgarian: Wonder if Landen's around... I want to up my carving technique, and he's the expert.

english: Better in here, I bet!
french: On est mieux ici, hein ?
russian: У нас-то точно лучше!
bulgarian: Better in here, I bet!

english: How's the weather out there?
french: Alors, que penses-tu du temps ?
russian: Как там на улице?
bulgarian: How's the weather out there?

english: But I'm sure there are even better days ahead! It's just a matter of time.
french: Mais je suis persuadé que des jours encore meilleurs nous attendent ! Ce n'est qu'une question de temps.
russian: Но я уверен, лучшие дни впереди! Это лишь вопрос времени.
bulgarian: But I'm sure there are even better days ahead! It's just a matter of time.

english: It's true the town's seen better days... The shop, too.
french: Il est vrai que la ville a connu des jours meilleurs... Le magasin aussi.
russian: Что правда, то правда — город знавал времена и получше... Как и магазин.
bulgarian: It's true the town's seen better days... The shop, too.

english: Thought about it myself, but I live too much by the seed of my plants.
french: Un temps, j'y avais songé, mais on n'a pas toujours le champ libre dans la vie.
russian: Я сам думал об этом, но сажать я умею только себя на диван.
bulgarian: Thought about it myself, but I live too much by the seed of my plants.

english: You know [Ari], I admire that you've taken over the old farm...
french: Tu sais, [Ari]. Je t'admire vraiment d'avoir repris cette vieille ferme...
russian:
Знаешь, [Ari], я уважаю, что ты

взялись

взяласьвзялсявзялось за старую ферму...
bulgarian: You know [Ari], I admire that you've taken over the old farm...

english: I'm the one in town who's known for being corny!
french: Je suis le type le plus terre-à-terre de cette ville !
russian: Я могу не только в огороде, но и вообще на ровном месте что-то ПОСЕЯТЬ.
bulgarian: I'm the one in town who's known for being corny!

english: I know you're the new farmer and all, but don't get jealous...
french: Je sais que c'est toi qui t'occupes de la ferme maintenant, et je ne veux pas créer de rivalité entre nous, mais...
russian: Понимаю, ты теперь местный фермер, но не завидуй...
bulgarian: I know you're the new farmer and all, but don't get jealous...

english: She's at that age...
french: Elle est arrivée à cet âge...
russian: У неё сейчас такой возраст...
bulgarian: She's at that age...

english: You know. Moving out on her own, trying to figure out her own path...
french: Tu sais, quand on part de chez ses parents et qu'on essaie de trouver sa voie...
russian: Ну, знаешь: переезд от родителей, поиск своего пути в жизни...
bulgarian: You know. Moving out on her own, trying to figure out her own path...

english: It isn't easy to chase your dreams.
french: Ce n'est pas facile de réaliser ses rêves.
russian: Идти к своей мечте всегда непросто.
bulgarian: It isn't easy to chase your dreams.

english: She could use a friend like you to encourage her...
french: On a toujours besoin d'un<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they> ami<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they> pour nous soutenir...
russian: Ей не хватает друзей вроде тебя...
bulgarian: She could use a friend like you to encourage her...

english: I beleaf the two of you could be a couple of peas in a pod!
french: Je parie que tu sauras l'aider à cultiver son jardin.
russian: Я цве-точно знаю, вы будете не разлей вода!
bulgarian: I beleaf the two of you could be a couple of peas in a pod!

english: Thanks for making time for Celine when you can, [Ari].
french: Merci de passer du temps avec Céline, [Ari].
russian: Спасибо, что уделяешь время Селин, когда можешь, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thanks for making time for Celine when you can, [Ari].

english: We sometimes get a little water in the store on days like this.
french: Il arrive qu'un peu d'eau entre dans le magasin, par des journées pareilles.
russian: В такие дни к нам в магазин иногда набирается немного воды.
bulgarian: We sometimes get a little water in the store on days like this.

english: It's true what they say... when it rains, it pours!
french: Quand ça tombe, ça tombe à seaux, comme on dit !
russian: Правду говорят... пришла беда — отворяй ворота!
bulgarian: It's true what they say... when it rains, it pours!

english: Watch your step, [Ari]!
french: Attention où tu mets les pieds, [Ari] !
russian: Смотри под ноги, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Watch your step, [Ari]!

english: It's not easy keeping the town well-stocked! But Nora gets the best for Mistria.
french: Approvisionner une ville n'est pas une tâche facile, mais Nora ne fait venir que les meilleurs produits à Mistria.
russian: Обеспечивать город товарами — нелёгкое дело! Но Нора для Мистрии всегда достаёт лучшее.
bulgarian: It's not easy keeping the town well-stocked! But Nora gets the best for Mistria.

english: I wonder what soup they've got going over at the Inn.
french: Je me demande quelle est la soupe du jour, à l'auberge.
russian: Интересно, какой суп сегодня в трактире?
bulgarian: I wonder what soup they've got going over at the Inn.

english: Now, on the topic of animals... what's Dell's newest favorite? Alpaca? Capybara?
french: Puisqu'on parle d'animaux, je me demande quel est l'animal préféré de Dell, en ce moment... L'alpaga ? Ou le capybara ?
russian: Кстати, о животных... Кто у Делл теперь любимчик? Альпаки? Капибары?
bulgarian: Now, on the topic of animals... what's Dell's newest favorite? Alpaca? Capybara?

english: It's so relaxing to get a bit of wood and whittle away!
french: Sculpter des animaux en bois, ça me détend à coup sûr !
russian: Так приятно взять дерево и вырезать, забыв обо всём!
bulgarian: It's so relaxing to get a bit of wood and whittle away!

english: I like to sneak some whittling in when I can... I've been working on forest animals lately.
french: Quand j'ai un peu de temps pour moi, j'aime bien m'adonner à la sculpture sur bois... Je suis dans ma période des animaux de la forêt, en ce moment.
russian: Иногда получается выкроить время на вырезку — сейчас работаю над зверушками из леса.
bulgarian: I like to sneak some whittling in when I can... I've been working on forest animals lately.

english: Business keeps up in the winter, too. Mistria's a busy town!
french: Même en hiver, les affaires sont florissantes. La vie à Mistria ne s'arrête jamais !
russian: Зимой торговля тоже идёт. Мистрия — город деловой!
bulgarian: Business keeps up in the winter, too. Mistria's a busy town!

english: And I tell you, it's snow joke!
french: Il ne faudrait pas qu'on nous prenne pour un glacier !
russian: Не лёдкое дело, знаешь ли!
bulgarian: And I tell you, it's snow joke!

english: It's my job to get the ice off of the General Store's windows!
french: C'est moi qui suis chargé de dégivrer les vitrines du magasin.
russian: Мне нужно очистить окна лавки ото льда.
bulgarian: It's my job to get the ice off of the General Store's windows!

english: Thank you for the birthday gift, [Ari]!
french: Merci pour le cadeau d'anniversaire, [Ari] !
russian: Спасибо за подарок на день рождения, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Thank you for the birthday gift, [Ari]!

english: Ooh! No time like the present for a present!
french: Oh ! Rien ne vaut le temps présent pour un présent !
russian: Ооо! Нет лучшего гостя, чем с гостинцем!
bulgarian: Ooh! No time like the present for a present!

english: Well... they say not to look a gift horse in the mouth...
french: Comme on dit... « À cadeau donné, on ne regarde pas les dents. »
russian: Ну... Дарёному коню в зубы не смотрят...
bulgarian: Well... they say not to look a gift horse in the mouth...

english: It's just what I needed to gift my spirits!
french: Avec toi, les cadeaux, c'est l'eldorado.
russian: То что нужно, чтобы поднять мне настроение!
bulgarian: It's just what I needed to gift my spirits!

english: Thanks, [Ari], I really like this!
french: Merci, [Ari], ça me plaît beaucoup !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari], мне очень нравится!
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari], I really like this!

english: You're a pro at producing produce! Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Dans ton genre, t'es un cador des cadeaux ! Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Ты просто про в продуцировании продукции! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: You're a pro at producing produce! Thanks, [Ari]!

english: You're a peach! I'm so grape-ful, thank you berry much!
french: C'est chou ! Tout ça pour un vieux hibou roux comme moi !
russian: Ты просто облачко! Я очень влаго-дарен! Спасибо о-гром-ное!
bulgarian: You're a peach! I'm so grape-ful, thank you berry much!

english: Thank you, [Ari]! This is so thoughtful.
french: Merci, [Ari] ! C'est vraiment chic de ta part.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]. Это очень обдуманно.
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]! This is so thoughtful.

english: Wow, is this really for me? I love it!
french: Waouh, c'est pour moi ? J'adore !
russian: Ого, это мне? Как здорово!
bulgarian: Wow, is this really for me? I love it!

english: [Ari], you're so gifted at giving gifts! It's like you're always present in the moment.
french: [Ari], ça te connaît, le plaisir d'offrir ! Moi, c'est la joie de recevoir !
russian:
[Ari], ты просто

одарены

одаренаодарёнодарено дарить подарки! Ты никогда не боишься презентовать себя.
bulgarian: [Ari], you're so gifted at giving gifts! It's like you're always present in the moment.

english: Oho, this looks delicious! Thank you, [Ari], I love it!
french: Oh, ça a l'air délicieux ! Merci, [Ari]. J'adore !
russian: Ого, на вид — просто объеденье! Спасибо, [Ari], мне очень нравится!
bulgarian: Oho, this looks delicious! Thank you, [Ari], I love it!

english: This is going to hit the spot! Bullseye, [Ari]!
french: Tu choisis toujours pile ce que j'aime ! Encore une fois dans le mille, [Ari] !
russian: Это то что нужно! В яблочко, [Ari]!
bulgarian: This is going to hit the spot! Bullseye, [Ari]!

english: Thanks, [Ari]! I'll turn this into something tasty later!
french: Merci, [Ari] ! J'en ferai quelque chose de délicieux plus tard !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]! Сделаю из этого что-нибудь вкусное попозже!
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari]! I'll turn this into something tasty later!

english: Well, thanks!
french: Ah, merci !
russian: Ох, спасибо!
bulgarian: Well, thanks!

english: I don't think I get the joke, [Ari].
french: Je crois que je n'ai pas compris ta blague, [Ari].
russian: Я не понял шутки, [Ari].
bulgarian: I don't think I get the joke, [Ari].

english: Have you tried some of Darcy's iced herbals? It's one of her special-teas!
french: Tu as déjà goûté les tisanes glacées de Darcy ? C'est une de ses spéciali-thés !
russian:
Ты

пробовали

пробовалапробовалпробовало холодные чаи со специями у Дарси? Это её специи-альность!
bulgarian: Have you tried some of Darcy's iced herbals? It's one of her special-teas!

english: Darcy's coffee runs out quickly, so don't be shy... you wouldn't want to be latte to the party.
french: Le café de Darcy part à toute vitesse, alors fais comme le citron... presse-toi.
russian: Кофе у Дарси уходит очень быстро, так что не скромничай... Ты же не хочешь оказаться копушино?
bulgarian: Darcy's coffee runs out quickly, so don't be shy... you wouldn't want to be latte to the party.

english: [Ari], are you here to try some of Darcy's coffees? They're fa-brew-lous!
french: [Ari], tu as déjà goûté un des cafés de Darcy ? Ils passent crème !
russian: [Ari], ты здесь попробовать кофе от Дарси? Оно велико-бленд-но!
bulgarian: [Ari], are you here to try some of Darcy's coffees? They're fa-brew-lous!

english: Last time Dell got coffee, it resulted in... The Incident. Let me tell you, it caused a latte problems!
french: La dernière fois que Dell a bu un café, ça lui est monté au cerveau. C'était la ca-tasse-trophe !
russian: В прошлый раз когда Делл выпила кофе, произошла... ситуация. Проблемы были большие, но больше я не скажу: я же не трипло!
bulgarian: Last time Dell got coffee, it resulted in... The Incident. Let me tell you, it caused a latte problems!

english: Louis is always teasing my choice of footwear, but dads in sandals are a time-honored tradition. Anything else would be sandal-ous.
french: Louis se moque toujours de mes sandales alors que c'est un art de vivre. Le premier qui me dit le contraire, je fais un sandale !
russian: Луи постоянно придирается к моему выбору обуви, но бати должны носить сандали, это традиция. Любая другая обувь вызовет настоящий сандал!
bulgarian: Louis is always teasing my choice of footwear, but dads in sandals are a time-honored tradition. Anything else would be sandal-ous.

english: Because he believes in sole mates!
french: Parce qu'il n'en a rien à cirer !
russian: Потому что он верит, что два сапога — пара!
bulgarian: Because he believes in sole mates!

english: Hey [Ari], you know why Louis makes his shoes in pairs?
french: Hé, [Ari], tu sais pourquoi Louis ne vend pas beaucoup de chaussures ?
russian: Эй, [Ari], знаешь, почему Луи делает обувь парами?
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], you know why Louis makes his shoes in pairs?

english: Louis can design, sew and knit... he's a triple thread.
french: Louis sait coudre, broder et tricoter... Il a plus d'un fil à son aiguille !
russian: Луи может и дизайн придумать, и сшить, и поткать... и у него всё связано!
bulgarian: Louis can design, sew and knit... he's a triple thread.

english: Who knew fashion designers were so clothes-minded?
french: Mais il n'en a que faire... à repasser !
russian: Подумать только: у портных столько работы, что они всегда зашиваются!
bulgarian: Who knew fashion designers were so clothes-minded?

english: I'm always giving Louis ideas for new clothing, but he always ignores me.
french: Je donne toujours des idées de tenue à Louis.
russian: Я всё время подаю Луи разные идеи для новых нарядов, но он эти наряды не принимает.
bulgarian: I'm always giving Louis ideas for new clothing, but he always ignores me.

english: Jo's always buying up all of Merri's restored furniture... I keep telling her there are already plenty of places to sit at the Inn, but she couldn't chair less.
french: Jo achète plein de meubles à Merri... Je lui dis toujours qu'il y a assez de chaises à l'auberge, mais elle s'assied sur mes conseils.
russian: Джо постоянно покупает у Мэрри отреставрированную мебель... Я ей говорю, что в трактире и так полно мест, куда можно сесть, но она предпочитает стоять. На своём!
bulgarian: Jo's always buying up all of Merri's restored furniture... I keep telling her there are already plenty of places to sit at the Inn, but she couldn't chair less.

english: Merri's got a new bed frame for sale... Nora says ours is good enough, but I like this one bedder...
french: Merri vend un nouveau cadre de lit... Nora dit que le nôtre est en bon état, mais moi, je ne peux plus l'encadrer...
russian: У Мэрри в продаже новая койка... Нора говорит, что наша и так хороша, но она мне кой-как...
bulgarian: Merri's got a new bed frame for sale... Nora says ours is good enough, but I like this one bedder...

english: Nora wants a new desk for her accounting... that's quite understan-table.
french: Nora aimerait un nouveau bureau pour faire sa compta... Je ne sais pas si c'est un bon calcul.
russian: Нора хочет купить новый письменный стол, чтобы вести бухгалтерию... С этим нужно считаться.
bulgarian: Nora wants a new desk for her accounting... that's quite understan-table.

english: [Ari], I'm gonna shoot straight with you... Merri's got great couches and I've got a great pun about being king of them, but Nora forbade me to say it.
french: Tu sais, [Ari]... Merri vend de superbes canapés, mais Nora m'a interdit d'en parler... « sofa » toi !
russian: [Ari], скажу прямо... У Мэрри в продаже много отличных диванов, а у меня как раз есть отличная шутка про короля диванов, но Нора запретила мне ее рассказывать.
bulgarian: [Ari], I'm gonna shoot straight with you... Merri's got great couches and I've got a great pun about being king of them, but Nora forbade me to say it.

english: You know, [Ari], I almost became a psychic myself. I gave it up, though... couldn't see any future in it.
bulgarian: You know, [Ari], I almost became a psychic myself. I gave it up, though... couldn't see any future in it.

english: The number of customers Stillwell gets is impressive... he surely makes a tidy prophet.
bulgarian: The number of customers Stillwell gets is impressive... he surely makes a tidy prophet.

english: Stillwell is always muttering about darkness or wailing about darkness... he's never a happy medium.
bulgarian: Stillwell is always muttering about darkness or wailing about darkness... he's never a happy medium.

english: Do you ever get the feeling that Stillwell only sees the worst in things? He's pretty pessi-mystic.
bulgarian: Do you ever get the feeling that Stillwell only sees the worst in things? He's pretty pessi-mystic.

english: But it didn't work! I got creamed!
french: Rien à faire ! Monsieur fait la fine bouche.
russian: Но ему всё равно, он взбил меня, как сливки!
bulgarian: But it didn't work! I got creamed!

english: I tried to butter up Taliferro before entering his $Cooking Challenge$...
french: J'ai voulu amadouer cette andouille de Taliferro avant le $défi gastronomique$...
russian: Я пытался подмаслить Талиферро перед тем, как подался на $смотр блюд$...
bulgarian: I tried to butter up Taliferro before entering his $Cooking Challenge$...

english: But I got fried! Deep fried, even!
french: Au final, je me suis pris une sacrée gamelle.
russian: Но получил прожарку! Я бы даже сказал, глубокую прожарку!
bulgarian: But I got fried! Deep fried, even!

english: I was simmering with excitement to join this week's $Cooking Challenge$...
french: Je bouillais de participer au $défi gastronomique$ de la semaine...
russian: Я так ждал отзыва Талиферро на $смотре блюд$, просто кипел от волнения...
bulgarian: I was simmering with excitement to join this week's $Cooking Challenge$...

english: Unfortunately, I got berried!
french: Malheureusement, ça a tourné en eau de boudin.
russian: Но Талиферро разгрушил мои надежды!
bulgarian: Unfortunately, I got berried!

english: I was feeling peachy about entering the newest $Cooking Challenge$...
french: J'avais une de ces patates avant le nouveau $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro...
russian: Я думал, что на этом $смотре блюд$ всё будет в шоколаде...
bulgarian: I was feeling peachy about entering the newest $Cooking Challenge$...

english: Put me in an oven and call me a meringue!
french: Je ne devais vraiment pas être dans mon assiette.
russian: Я выжат, как лимон, и разбит, как яйцо!
bulgarian: Put me in an oven and call me a meringue!

english: No eggscuses, I got whipped by Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$!
french: Inutile de tourner autour du pot ! J'ai fait chou blanc au $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro !
russian: На этом $смотре блюд$ меня уделали, как котлету!
bulgarian: No eggscuses, I got whipped by Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$!

english: Vera says she's got blue dye in stock! What do you think, should I go for it?
french: Vera dit qu'elle a de la coloration bleue dans ses cartons ! Tu crois que ça m'irait ?
russian: Вера говорит, у нее есть синяя краска для волос. Как думаешь, стоит мне попробовать?
bulgarian: Vera says she's got blue dye in stock! What do you think, should I go for it?

english: Luckily Vera's handy with a razor. She really shaved me some trouble!
french: Heureusement que Vera a bien voulu me la raser, j'étais à un poil de me faire larguer !
russian: К счастью, Вера отлично владеет бритвой и все проблемы как лезвием срубает!
bulgarian: Luckily Vera's handy with a razor. She really shaved me some trouble!

english: I tried to grow a beard, but Nora didn't like it...
french: Je me suis laissé pousser la barbe une fois, mais ça ne plaisait pas à Nora...
russian: Я пытался отрастить бороду, но Норе не понравилось...
bulgarian: I tried to grow a beard, but Nora didn't like it...

english: She knows all the short cuts. Long cuts, too, if you prefer the scenic route!
french: C'est l'exp'hair-te en coiffure. Elle a l'esprit créa-tif !
russian: Она знает, где лучше всего срезать. Или нарастить, если предпочитаешь длинные прогулки.
bulgarian: She knows all the short cuts. Long cuts, too, if you prefer the scenic route!

english: If you need a haircut or you need directions, Vera's got you covered...
french: Si tu as besoin d'une coupe de cheveux ou de conseils, va voir Vera...
russian: Если тебе нужна стрижка или узнать, как куда пройти, это всё к Вере...
bulgarian: If you need a haircut or you need directions, Vera's got you covered...

english: Would you believe it, it turned orange!
french: Et crois-le ou non, ils ont viré au roux !
russian: Не поверишь, они стали рыжими!
bulgarian: Would you believe it, it turned orange!

english: I once had Vera bleach my hair...
french: Un jour, j'ai demandé à Vera de me décolorer les cheveux...
russian: Я как-то попросил Веру осветлить мои волосы...
bulgarian: I once had Vera bleach my hair...

english: I usually get a chuckle out of folks, but I never met someone who laughed too much at a pun.
french: J'arrive souvent à faire pouffer les gens, mais je n'avais jamais vu quelqu'un qui rigole trop à un jeu de mots.
russian: Обычно мне удаётся пробить людей на смешок, но до сих пор я не видел человека, который чересчур много смеётся.
bulgarian: I usually get a chuckle out of folks, but I never met someone who laughed too much at a pun.

english: It's just not that funny, pal!
french: Ce n'est quand même pas drôle à ce point !
russian: Это смешной каламбур, но не настолько же, парень!
bulgarian: It's just not that funny, pal!

english: I was just chatting with Wheedle, and I've got to say...
french: Je papotais avec Wheedle et c'est amusant.
russian: Недавно я болтал с Хлюстом и должен сказать...
bulgarian: I was just chatting with Wheedle, and I've got to say...

english: I appreciate when he says everything in his store is a deal, but I can't be dealing with an empty wallet.
french: Il a beau dire qu'il est le roi des bonnes affaires, je ne veux pas finir sans le sou.
russian: Приятно, что у него в лавке, по его словам, всё по скидке, только скидываться мне нечем!
bulgarian: I appreciate when he says everything in his store is a deal, but I can't be dealing with an empty wallet.

english: I'm just browsing at Wheedle's booth today.
french: Je jette un œil à ce que Wheedle propose sur son stand.
russian: Я сегодня рассматривал товары у Хлюста.
bulgarian: I'm just browsing at Wheedle's booth today.

english: On to burger and better things!
french: À moi les burgers et les nuggets !
russian: Вперёд за бургерами!
bulgarian: On to burger and better things!

english: That $Fast Food$ in Wheedle's shop looks tempting, but I should eat a proper meal...
french: L'$encas sur le pouce$ de Wheedle donne envie, mais je vais me limiter à un vrai repas...
russian: Фастфуд в лавке Хлюста выглядит заманчиво, но лучше поесть как следует...
bulgarian: That $Fast Food$ in Wheedle's shop looks tempting, but I should eat a proper meal...

english: Now I might be on the hook for a new set of windows at the General Store... don't tell Nora!
french: Je crois que j'ai signé pour remplacer les vitrines du magasin... Ne dis rien à Nora !
russian: Возможно, теперь я ввязался в обновление витрин для универмага... Только Норе не говори!
bulgarian: Now I might be on the hook for a new set of windows at the General Store... don't tell Nora!

english: I told Wheedle I was just doing some window-shopping and he told me he had a fine collection of windows for sale...
french: Quand j'ai dit à Wheedle que je faisais du lèche-vitrine, il m'a répondu qu'il avait de superbes baies en promotion...
russian: Я сказал Хлюсту, что просто глазею на его витрины. А он ответил, что как раз распродаёт отличный набор витрин...
bulgarian: I told Wheedle I was just doing some window-shopping and he told me he had a fine collection of windows for sale...

english: It's probably for the best, I don't think Nora would want Dell to hear that many puns in one song.
french: C'est sans doute mieux, d'ailleurs. Je crois que Nora n'aimerait pas que Dell entende tous les jeux de mots qu'il fait dans ses chansons.
russian: Впрочем, оно и к лучшему. Нора с ума сойдёт, если Делл услышит столько каламбуров в одной песне.
bulgarian: It's probably for the best, I don't think Nora would want Dell to hear that many puns in one song.

english: Zorel doesn't have anything by "Strange Albert". He's a comedian singer I really like from the Capital.
french: Zorel n'a rien en commun avec « L'Étrange Albert ». C'est un chanteur et comédien de la capitale que j'aime beaucoup.
russian: У Зорель в коллекции нет песен Странного Альберта. Это столичный певец-комик, я его очень люблю.
bulgarian: Zorel doesn't have anything by "Strange Albert". He's a comedian singer I really like from the Capital.

english: You're telling me... a Dragon forged that bracelet?
french: Ça voudrait dire... que ce bracelet a été forgé par un dragon ?
russian: Ты хочешь сказать, что... этот браслет ковал дракон?
bulgarian: You're telling me... a Dragon forged that bracelet?

english: Oh... it did? I see. Carry on...
french: Oh... Vraiment ? Je vois. Continue...
russian: А... правда? Ясно, пойду дальше...
bulgarian: Oh... it did? I see. Carry on...

english: I was by the Museum and took a peek inside! I saw that $Dragon Forged Bracelet$.
french: En passant près du musée, j'ai jeté un coup d'œil à l'intérieur et j'ai vu le $bracelet de forge-dragon$.
russian: Я проходил мимо музея и решил заглянуть на минутку. Там был $браслет драконьей ковки$.
bulgarian: I was by the Museum and took a peek inside! I saw that $Dragon Forged Bracelet$.

english: And she said I was frying her patience!
french: Elle m'a dit que ça lui avait donné la frite !
russian: И она сказала, что запахло жареным!
bulgarian: And she said I was frying her patience!

english: I'm so proud.
french: Je suis si fier d'elle.
russian: Горжусь своей дочкой.
bulgarian: I'm so proud.

english: I told Celine a joke about the $Hot Potato$ at the Museum...
french: J'ai raconté une blague à Céline sur la $patate chaude$ du musée...
russian: Когда мы с Селин были в музее, я пошутил про $горячую картошку$...
bulgarian: I told Celine a joke about the $Hot Potato$ at the Museum...

english: Don't know if I share its tastes, though. Maybe I should give it a shot!
french: C'est une expression de jeune, ne me demande pas ce que ça veut dire !
russian: Хотя не уверен, что разделяю её вкус. Может, стоит попробовать?
bulgarian: Don't know if I share its tastes, though. Maybe I should give it a shot!

english: I feel a kinship with that $Loam Caterpillar$ at the Museum! I'm also an appreciator of a good loam.
french: Je me sens un peu comme la $chenille des terres$ du musée. Moi aussi, je suis « déter ».
russian: В музее я почувствовал некоторое родство с $глиноедкой$! Я тоже ценю качественные почвы.
bulgarian: I feel a kinship with that $Loam Caterpillar$ at the Museum! I'm also an appreciator of a good loam.

english: The fact that I can go see it at the Museum- well, I'm lichen it a lot!
french: De pouvoir la contempler au musée, c'est une grande émoussion !
russian: Теперь можно просто пойти и посмотреть на него в музее. Раньше я так не мох!
bulgarian: The fact that I can go see it at the Museum- well, I'm lichen it a lot!

english: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the =Narrows Moss= at the Museum. You may not know it, but I'm a bit of a moss expert, and that moss is very rare and unique!
french: Je n'en croyais pas mes yeux quand j'ai vu de la =mousse des mines= au musée. On ne dirait pas, mais je suis expert en la matière et celle-ci est vraiment très rare !
russian: Глазам не поверил, когда увидел =мох ущелья= в музее. Может, и не скажешь, но я немного моховик... В смысле знаток мха! И этот — редкий экземпляр.
bulgarian: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the =Narrows Moss= at the Museum. You may not know it, but I'm a bit of a moss expert, and that moss is very rare and unique!
